description: The National Network of Regional Coastal Monitoring Programmes brings together six regional programmes in England, each led by a local authority, that collect coastal monitoring data in a coordinated and systematic way for coastal engineering and management. Funding comes from Defra in five-year cycles through the Environment Agency, and the data underpins strategic and local flood and coastal erosion risk management decisions. The website, run by the Channel Coastal Observatory, also hosts data for the Welsh Coastal Monitoring Centre. It offers survey data and reports by region, and a real-time data service with wave buoys, tide gauges, meteorological stations and GPS data, shown on a map and in tables, with an API key for direct access, an alerts system and a Google Earth file for the buoys. Data access is free, with registration for downloads and the API; no licence is named, and the disclaimer says data is provided as is. Caveats: survey types and dates differ between regions. Coverage is the coast of England and Wales. It supports coastal flood and erosion hazard analysis for sea defences, ports and coastal infrastructure; there are no related records in the catalogue yet.
